correctness.rationale: The proof independently identifies the seven-dimensional radical as the full nonzero zero-divisor set, writes the multiplication product in degrees 2 and 3, and derives the projective point/line and point-scalar clique blocks. The real adjacency operator decomposes into internal -1 subspaces, repeated point-scalar c-1 subspaces, and 2m+1 quotient coordinates. Projective-plane incidence NN^T=qI+J yields an (m-1)-fold quadratic and one 3x3 cubic, with all dimensions summing to q^7-1. The symbolic expression for det(T) is strictly negative for every q>=2, and the remaining factors are nonzero at zero. The actual included checker passed 8001 exhaustive unordered pairs for q=2; q=4 and q=8 independent finite-field product samples; all incidence identities; class sizes; and the q=2 full 127-eigenvalue numerical comparison. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Source and assertion-level comparisons found no statement that gives, directly or by a stronger theorem, the complete ordinary simple adjacency characteristic polynomial for the non-chain local group algebra k[(C_2)^3] over every characteristic-two finite field. The most relevant inspected group-ring paper establishes diameter, girth and group-recognition results, while a later spectral treatment explicitly evaluates different classes of rings. Three close public research documents address a different bivariate cubic algebra, modular graph minimum degree, and bilinear zero-product determination. The exact spectral factorization and its universal nonsingularity survive those implication comparisons. Priority remains qualified by possible unlocated generalized treatments.
residual_risks: A stronger general zero-divisor-graph or compressed spectral theorem not returned by search could imply the explicit family.
Some spectral papers were checked by abstract or scoped statements rather than full text; titles of plausible nonsemisimple generalizations may be missed.
The finite computations are corroboration, not a proof of the all-q identity.

value.rationale: The standard modular group-ring zero-divisor graph is a motivated object of 2014 literature. Determining its complete q-uniform graph structure and adjacency characteristic polynomial for the rank-three elementary abelian two-group algebra is a natural extension beyond known diameter, group-recovery, and minimum-degree invariants. The projective-plane incidence identification and universal real nonsingularity are substantive structural results for an infinite family, not a small table or arbitrary parameter tweak.
